newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB says independence still optimal solution.
newsitem.headline: SNB says independence still optimal solution.

text.p: Hans Meyer, president of the Swiss National Bank (SNB), said an independent monetary policy was still the optimal solution for Switzerland because it is difficult to gauge whether a Big Brother -- either Germany or EMU -- would stick to the same goals that the SNB has.

Meyer said in an interview with the Basler Zeitung that he welcomed the concept of a stability pact for European countries as a way to solve the issue of what will happen to the convergence criteria of members in the third stage of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) 10 years down the road.
However, he cautioned that institutional measures could not control financial conduct unless politicians are willing to.
Meyer repeated that the SNB is basically faced with two alternatives if the Swiss franc were to rise excessively.
One was to find a "Big Brother" with the main problem being finding which one has the same route of march.
"But that might even be conceivable. But it would be much more difficult to judge whether he would stick to this route," Meyer said, adding.
"The difficulty in answering this question makes the other alternative -- the relative independence -- so attractive. That's why we have chosen it and still think it is the optimal solution."
